title: The brain bot

story: Monday morning. A backend engineer who joined last week writes in #engineering: "@Rhino Brain how does a code run reach the on-prem client?" The first version of the bot, a Claude session with a good prompt and access to the brain pages, answers in five seconds, in a friendly tone: "The cloud opens a gRPC connection to each client and sends the code run down it. Source: rnd-kb/engineering/cloud-to-client.md."

Both halves are wrong. The client opens the connection, because customer networks accept no connections from outside, and there is no page with that name: the model wrote a path that looks like a brain path. The prompt already said "only cite pages you have read", and the model obeys that almost every time. But almost every time, in a channel that all of R&D reads, means a few wrong answers a week, and each one comes with a source that makes it look checked.
hook.question: How do we build a Slack bot whose answers rest only on sources that really exist, without trusting the model to be honest about them?

p: Four things are involved: Slack, the bot's own code, an agent session, and two mirrors. Slack delivers the mention. The bot's code is a Bolt for Python app in Socket Mode, the same pattern as Nova's Slack app: the app opens a websocket connection out to Slack, so it needs no public address and nobody on the internet can call it. For each question the code starts one Agent SDK session, a Claude conversation that can use tools, and the session reads two mirrors: read-only git copies of the brain repo, rnd-kb, and the product repo, fcp, which a small helper refreshes every 10 minutes.

The session gets as little power as an answer needs. Its tools are Read, Grep and Glob, so it can open and search files, and nothing else: no shell, no writes, no web. setting_sources=[] means it loads no settings or CLAUDE.md files from disk, so its whole behaviour comes from the prompt file we ship. It runs on Sonnet 5.5 at low effort, with one line in the prompt that you met in the kb skill: search even when you feel sure. Every model call goes to our LLM gateway, which adds the bot's key, so the pod itself holds no Anthropic key. And the model never talks to Slack. It returns its answer to our code, and our code decides what gets posted.

The bot is written in Python, while the rest of the agent platform is TypeScript, for one reason: it imports kb_tools, the brain's Python package, inside its own process. So the bot ranks pages and removes sensitive words exactly the way the kb command and BRAIN-QA do, and the nightly test measures the same code that answers people.

code.text:
# rnd-kb-tooling/bot/app.py (part 1). Runs on inf-rhinohealth; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is the LLM gateway (it adds the key).
import asyncio
import os

from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage, query
from slack_bolt.adapter.socket_mode.async_handler import AsyncSocketModeHandler
from slack_bolt.async_app import AsyncApp

from bot.citations import ANSWER, format_reply, keep_resolvable  # ANSWER: {answer, citations, unverified} schema
from kb_tools.scan import has_blocked_terms, redact  # same PHI patterns and deny-list as kb-lint

app = AsyncApp(token=os.environ["SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"])
CHANNELS = set(os.environ["BRAIN_CHANNELS"].split(","))  # public engineering channels only (DATA-SCOPE.md)
OPTIONS = ClaudeAgentOptions(
    model="claude-sonnet-5-5", effort="low",
    cwd="/mirror/rnd-kb", add_dirs=["/mirror/fcp"],  # read-only git mirrors, refreshed every 10 minutes
    tools=["Read", "Grep", "Glob"], setting_sources=[],  # no Bash, no writes, no web, no local config
    system_prompt=open("/app/prompts/brain.md").read(),
    output_format={"type": "json_schema", "schema": ANSWER})

notes.text: The same scan the brain's lint uses: patient-like data and the deny-list of customer names.
Channel IDs, not names, of the public engineering channels the data scope allows.
Sonnet 5.5 at low effort: brain questions are short, and the search does most of the work.
The session starts in the brain mirror and may also read the fcp mirror.
Three read-only tools, and no settings from disk.
The answer must be JSON in the shape of ANSWER. The next section explains why.

deeper.h: Go deeper: why our own bot
p: Anthropic has its own Slack app for Claude, but it is not available under our zero data retention agreement, the contract that says Anthropic does not keep our prompts. So the brain bot is our own small app, with the same brain and the same citation rule as everything else that reads it.

read.h: Ask for an answer that code can read
p: To check citations, our code first has to find them. In free text a source can hide anywhere: in brackets, at the end, as a link, half in a sentence. So the session asks for structured output, which means the model must answer with JSON that matches a JSON schema we give it. Our schema, ANSWER, has three fields: answer, the text for people; citations, a list of sources, each written the way kb search prints them, rnd-kb/<path>@<sha>; and unverified, a list of claims the model makes but could not tie to a source.

The SDK hands that JSON back as structured_output on the final message. Now the citations are a list our code can walk through, one item at a time, and the model's own words cannot blur what counts as a source.

code.text:
# rnd-kb-tooling/bot/citations.py: the bot's citation wall
"""Only sources that really exist in the mirror reach Slack."""
import re
import subprocess

MIRRORS = {"rnd-kb": "/mirror/rnd-kb", "fcp": "/mirror/fcp"}  # read-only git mirrors in the pod
I_DONT_KNOW = "I don't know. Ask in #engineering, or run kb search yourself."

ANSWER = {  # the JSON schema the model must answer in
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "answer": {"type": "string"},
        "citations": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},  # rnd-kb/<path>@<sha>
        "unverified": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
    },
    "required": ["answer", "citations", "unverified"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
}

notes.text: Where each repo prefix of a citation lives inside the pod.
The reply when no source survives: an honest answer, and where to ask a person.
One string per source, for example rnd-kb/engineering/code-run-path.md@841d4a5.
No extra fields, so the model cannot put sources somewhere our code does not look.

read.h: Check every citation against the mirror
p: Here is the wall that would have stopped Monday's answer. For each citation, our code splits it into the repo, the path and the sha, and asks git one question: does this file exist at this commit in the mirror? The command is git cat-file -e <sha>:<path>, which prints nothing and only answers with its exit code. A made-up page fails, because no commit has it. A made-up commit fails too. A citation that resolves stays. When no citation is left, the reply becomes "I don't know" and where to ask, because an honest gap is better than a fluent mistake.

Notice that the check uses the commit named in the citation, not the newest one. If an owner renames a page an hour later, the old citation still resolves, and that is correct: it names exactly what the session read, and anyone can open that text with git show <sha>:<path>. It also means that the mirror refreshing while a session works does not throw away good sources.

Look at what this check does not do. It proves that the source exists; it does not prove that the source says what the answer claims. That is a harder problem, and the deeper panel shows how the bot handles it for hard questions.

notes.text: Called once per citation.
rpartition splits at the last @, so the path itself may contain any characters.
An unknown repo or something that is not a sha is refused before git runs.
Exit code 0 means git knows this file at this commit.
No source survived, so the answer is replaced, not just stripped of its sources.
The reply people see: the answer, its sources, and any claim the model could not check.

deeper.h: Go deeper: hard questions and a checker
p: Most questions need one page. Some cross code, tickets and pages, like "why did we stop running backend CI on drafts?", and one quick pass tends to guess. So a cheap router call (Haiku 5.5 at low effort, with structured output) labels each question simple or hard. Simple ones stay on the path above. Hard ones run on Sonnet 5.5 at high effort with the Agent tool, which lets the session start helpers: subagents with their own prompt, model and tools. A code reader and a kb reader search the mirrors with Read, Grep and Glob, and a Jira reader uses a small search tool written in our own code, so the Jira token stays in our process and never enters a prompt. Helpers return pointers (file:line, path@sha or a ticket key), not essays.

Then a checker, a separate helper on Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort, re-reads every cited source and keeps a claim only if the source really says it. Claims it cannot confirm go into unverified, so the reply shows them as not checked instead of dropping them without a word. The fan-out costs more per answer, so it stays only if ten hard questions in BRAIN-QA's nightly run show that correctness goes up. And when someone reacts with a thumbs-down to a reply, the bot opens an issue in rnd-kb with the question, the answer and the cited pages, assigned to the page's owner from OWNERS.yml, because a bad answer usually means a page that is wrong or missing.

read.h: Walls before and after the model
p: The citation check runs after the model. Two more walls stand around it, and they are in our code for the same reason: they must hold even if the model is fooled. Before any model call, the handler checks that the mention came from one of the allowed public channels, by channel ID, and that the text contains no patient-like data and no word from the deny-list, the list of customer names that must never appear. A question that fails gets one fixed sentence back. It costs nothing, and its text never reaches a prompt or a log of model calls.

After the model, the reply goes through redact(), which replaces deny-list words, and then our code posts it in the thread of the question. The model has no Slack tool at all, so a page or a question that tries to talk the model into posting somewhere else has nothing to work with.

notes.text: The session streams messages; the last one, the ResultMessage, carries the JSON answer.
The citation wall runs before anything else sees the answer.
Wall one: wrong channel or blocked words, refused before any model call.
thread_ts makes the reply a thread reply under the question.
After the call: format the checked answer, redact it, and our code posts it in the thread.
Socket Mode: the app dials out to Slack with the app-level token.

deeper.h: Go deeper: how the bot runs on inf
p: The bot runs on inf, our internal Kubernetes cluster, deployed the way n8n is: an image in our container registry with tags that cannot be moved, and a Terraform unit in the infrastructure repo that installs it with Helm. The image is pinned by digest, the hash of its content, so the running bot is exactly the one that passed CI. There is one replica, because Socket Mode holds one connection, and no Service or HTTP route, because nothing calls in.

A network policy lets the pod reach only Slack, GitHub, the Jira site and the LLM gateway. The Slack tokens, the brain's GitHub App key and a read-only Jira token come from Vault, our secret store; a person writes them there and a person applies the Terraform plan. If the pod restarts more than three times in an hour, an alert is sent to #ai-agents-alerts.

lab.title: A bot that can only cite what exists
lab.goal: Build the bot's citation wall and watch it turn a made-up source into "I don't know", keep a real one, and survive a page rename.

guess.q: The model answers with a citation to rnd-kb/engineering/cloud-to-client.md@<the mirror's current sha>. The sha is real, but the page has never existed. What does keep_resolvable do?

options.text: Keeps it, because the sha is a real commit.
options.why: The check asks for the file at that commit, not for the commit alone. No commit contains this file.

options.text: Drops it, and with no source left the reply becomes "I don't know" and where to ask.
options.why: git cat-file -e fails for a path that exists at no commit, and an answer with no surviving source is replaced.

options.text: Drops the citation but posts the answer text anyway.
options.why: That would post the wrong fact without any source, which is worse. With nothing left, the whole answer is replaced.

Set CHANNELS to {"C0ENGINEERING"}, a deny-list with one made-up customer, "Acme Health", and two patient-like patterns: a 9-digit number and the words MRN or DOB. Write has_blocked_terms(text), redact(text) and on_question(channel, text), which refuses with the fixed sentence before calling fake_answer(), a stand-in for the session that counts its calls and returns "At Acme Health, the on-prem client opens the stream to the cloud." solution.text:
"""The walls around the model call: refuse before asking, redact after, and our code posts."""
import re

CHANNELS = {"C0ENGINEERING"}  # BRAIN_CHANNELS: public engineering channels, by channel ID
DENY = ["Acme Health"]  # the real deny-list lives in Vault, never in a repo
PHI = [re.compile(r"\b\d{9}\b"), re.compile(r"\b(MRN|DOB)\b", re.IGNORECASE)]
REFUSAL = "I can't answer that here. Ask in a public engineering channel, without patient or customer details."
model_calls = 0


def has_blocked_terms(text: str) -> bool:
    return any(p.search(text) for p in PHI) or any(term.lower() in text.lower() for term in DENY)


def redact(text: str) -> str:
    for term in DENY:
        text = re.sub(re.escape(term), "[redacted]", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    return text


def fake_answer(question: str) -> str:  # stands in for answer(): one Agent SDK session
    global model_calls
    model_calls += 1
    return "At Acme Health, the on-prem client opens the stream to the cloud."


def on_question(channel: str, text: str) -> str:
    if channel not in CHANNELS or has_blocked_terms(text):
        return REFUSAL
    return redact(fake_answer(text))


print(on_question("C0ENGINEERING", "how does a code run reach the client?"))
print(on_question("C0RANDOMDM", "how does a code run reach the client?"))
print(on_question("C0ENGINEERING", "why did the run for patient 123456789 fail?"))
print("model calls:", model_calls)
# python3 walls.py
# At [redacted], the on-prem client opens the stream to the cloud.
# I can't answer that here. Ask in a public engineering channel, without patient or customer details.
# I can't answer that here. Ask in a public engineering channel, without patient or customer details.
# model calls: 1

check.q: The prompt already says "only cite pages you have read". Why does the bot still check every citation in code?

options.text: Because the prompt is ignored when structured output is on.
options.why: The prompt still works. The point is that it works almost always, and almost always is not enough in a channel all of R&D reads.

options.text: Because a prompt asks the model, while code decides: a rule in code holds even on the rare answer where the model gets it wrong.
options.why: The model obeys the prompt most of the time. The git check holds every time, and it does not depend on the model being honest.

options.text: Because Slack refuses replies without a verified link.
options.why: Slack posts any text. Checking sources is entirely our job.

check.q: A citation names rnd-kb/engineering/code-run-path.md at last week's commit. Since then the owner renamed the page. What does the bot do?

options.text: Drops it, because the file is not in the newest version of the mirror.
options.why: The check uses the commit named in the citation, and at that commit the file exists.

options.text: Replaces it with the new name automatically.
options.why: The bot never rewrites sources. It only keeps the ones that resolve.

options.text: Keeps it, because the file exists at that commit, and git show opens exactly the text that was read.
options.why: A path@sha citation is a fixed reference. A rename later does not make what was read untrue.

check.q: Someone asks the bot about a run "for patient 123456789" in an allowed channel. What happens?

options.text: The bot answers, then redacts the number from the reply.
options.why: Redacting the reply is too late: the question with the number would already have gone into a prompt.

options.text: The handler refuses with one fixed sentence before any model call.
options.why: The PHI check runs on the question first, so the text never reaches the model and the refusal costs nothing.

options.text: The model sees the number and decides to refuse.
options.why: That would depend on the model, and the text would already have left our process. The wall is in our code, before the call.

p: The bot lives in rnd-kb-tooling/bot/: app.py (Bolt for Python in Socket Mode and the Agent SDK for Python), citations.py and a prompt file with the line "search even when you feel sure". Walls in code: BRAIN_CHANNELS from the data scope in DATA-SCOPE.md, kb_tools.scan before the call, redact after it, and no reading of private channels. BRAIN-QA's answer mode points at answer(), with the targets of 85% retrieval and 80% correct. Hard questions add bot/hard.py: a Haiku 5.5 router, code-reader, kb-reader and jira-reader helpers on Haiku 5.5 at medium, a checker on Sonnet 5.5 at medium, an in-process read-only jira_search tool, and the thumbs-down issue through the rhino-kb GitHub App with issues:write.

The deploy follows the n8n units in the infrastructure repo: an rnd-kb-bot ECR repository with immutable tags in multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/artifacts/artifacts.hcl, and multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/brain-bot/ with brain-bot.hcl, secrets/ (owning the Vault path infrastructure/brain-bot) and repository/, which uses the agent-services helm_release module with one replica, an ExternalSecret from vault-store, two git-sync mirrors and expose = false. The plan runs locally over VPN and is pasted into the pull request; a person applies.

tickets.why: The bot itself: Socket Mode, the read-only session, structured output, the citation wall and the walls before and after the call.
Deploying it on inf like n8n: image by digest, Vault secrets, git mirrors, network policy, no public endpoint.
Hard questions: the router, the read-only helpers, the checker, and the thumbs-down issue for the page owner.

words.plain: A way for a Slack app to open its own connection to Slack, so it needs no public address.
Asking the model to answer with JSON that matches a schema, so code can read each field.
A source in the form rnd-kb/<path>@<sha>: one file at one commit, so anyone can open exactly what was read.
A read-only git copy of a repo next to the bot, refreshed every 10 minutes.
The list of customer names that must never appear in a prompt or a reply; it lives in Vault.

review.q: From memory, write the git command that tells you whether a citation resolves, and say what its exit code means.
review.a: git -C <mirror> cat-file -e <sha>:<path>. Exit code 0 means the file exists at that commit; anything else means the citation is dropped.

review.q: The model returns two citations: one resolves, one does not. What does the reply look like?
review.a: The answer with only the resolving source under Sources, plus any claims from unverified under Not checked. Only when no citation is left is the answer replaced by "I don't know".

review.q: Name the three walls around the model call and say which ones run before it.
review.a: Before: the channel allow-list and the PHI and deny-list scan of the question. After: the citation check and redact, and then our code posts; the model has no Slack tool.

remember: The model proposes an answer as JSON; our code keeps only the sources git can find at their commit, refuses sensitive questions before the call, and posts the reply itself.
